name: Malice
overview: Scripture reveals malice as a deep-rooted enmity that leads to destructive actions against others, beginning with the earliest human conflict when Cain rose up and killed his brother Abel. This hostility is further illustrated in the strained relationships within Abraham's family, as Sarah resented Hagar and her son, prompting their expulsion. The bitterness between Esau and Jacob highlights how malice can stem from jealousy and perceived injustice, with Esau harboring intentions to kill his brother. Additionally, Potiphar's wife's false accusations against Joseph demonstrate how malice can manifest in deceit and attempts to harm the innocent.
